question: Why do nurses use basic human needs as a guide in patient care?

options.B: To eliminate the need for doctors

explanation: Spot on! Basic needs give you a clear map to know which patient problems need your attention first. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h1)

question: As a nurse, why should you look beyond just the medical disease?

options.B: To treat the whole person effectively
options.C: To replace the medical treatment plan
options.D: To avoid writing detailed nursing notes

explanation: You got it! A patient is a human being, not just a disease diagnosis. Looking at their whole situation ensures they truly heal. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h1)

question: According to Maslow's pyramid, what sits right at the very bottom?
explanation: Correct! Things like air, food, and water are the foundation of survival. You can't build a house without a strong base! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h2)

question: What does Maslow's hierarchy tell us about lower-level needs?

options.A: They only matter in elderly patients
options.B: They are less important than self-esteem
options.C: They can be skipped during illness
options.D: They generally take priority over higher needs

explanation: Exactly! A hungry or suffocating patient won't care much about personal growth until their basic survival needs are met first. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which of these is a basic physiological need that a patient cannot live without?
explanation: Spot on! Oxygen is an immediate biological requirement for life. Without it, the body simply stops functioning. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h3)

question: Your patient is gasping for air and panicking. What is your very first move?
explanation: Brilliant! Breathing comes first above everything else. If the airway is blocked, other interventions can wait. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h3)

question: How do you protect a patient's physical safety while they are on the ward?
explanation: Correct! Keeping the ward safe from slips and falls is a daily duty that keeps patients out of extra trouble. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why is keeping a patient feeling psychologically safe so important in the hospital?

options.A: It lowers anxiety and supports healing
options.B: It guarantees a quick hospital discharge
options.C: It replaces the need for pain medication

explanation: You nailed it! A calm, reassured mind helps the body relax and heal faster. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is a major way to meet a patient's need for love and belonging?
explanation: Spot on! Human connection, love, and visits from dear ones make patients feel remembered and cherished. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which nursing action best shows support for a patient's psychosocial needs?

options.A: Isolating the patient to ensure complete quiet
options.B: Focusing solely on intravenous fluid rates
options.C: Welcoming family members to participate in care
options.D: Limiting all conversations to medical charts

explanation: Correct! Involving loved ones honors the patient's emotional ties and social support system. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h5)

question: In patient care, what does self-esteem mainly focus on?

options.D: Preventing accidental falls in the ward

explanation: You got it! Self-esteem is all about a person's dignity, self-worth, and feeling respected by others. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h6)

question: Your patient is recovering from a stroke and has shaky hands while eating. How can you boost their self-esteem?

options.A: Feeding them completely to save valuable time
options.B: Encouraging them to try while offering gentle support
options.C: Scolding them for spilling food on the bed
options.D: Asking a family member to take over all meals

explanation: Brilliant! Letting them do what they can protects their dignity and builds their confidence back up. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h6)

question: What factor heavily influences how a patient views their health, healing, and food?
explanation: Spot on! Cultural beliefs and religion shape how people view sickness, treatments, and what they can eat. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h7)

question: Why must nurses keep developmental stages in mind when looking at patient needs?

options.A: Needs change as a person grows from an infant to an adult
options.B: Adults and children always require identical medication dosages
options.D: Older adults do not experience physiological needs

explanation: Correct! A baby's needs look totally different from an adult's or an elderly person's needs. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is the very first step of the nursing process?
explanation: You got it! Assessment is where you gather all your facts and data about the patient's health status. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h8)

question: What happens during the evaluation phase of the nursing process?

options.A: Identifying potential risks for falls in the ward
options.B: Writing down the initial patient medical history
options.C: Checking if patient goals and needs have been met
options.D: Administering prescribed drugs to the patient

explanation: Spot on! Evaluation is where you check back to see if your nursing care actually helped the patient get better. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h8)
